description:
FILED s464a (Opus, 2026-09-02), found by a #964 probe and VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING
on a base worktree of a8b4043 (byte-identical output there), so it is not #964's
and did not block it.

PROBE (scratch p964/nest.pl; perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, same on the base commit
and on the #964 branch):

    package B1; sub steps { qw(a b) }
    package D1; our @ISA = ('B1'); sub steps { qw(x y), $_[0]->SUPER::steps }
    print join("|", D1->steps), "\n";
      perl  x|y|a|b
      PCL   ARRAY(0x1)|ARRAY(0x2)          <-- and both elements are wrong

    sub inner { (1,2) }  sub outer { (0, inner()) }
    print join("|", outer());     perl 0|1|2   PCL 0|ARRAY(0x3)
    my @a = (5,6);  sub outer2 { (4, @a) }
    print join("|", outer2());    perl 4|5|6   PCL 4|#S(p-flatten-marker :array #(5 6))
    sub inner3 { my @l=(7,8); @l }  sub outer3 { (6, inner3()) }
    print join("|", outer3());    perl 6|7|8   PCL 6|ARRAY(0x4)
    sub h { my %hh=(k=>1); %hh }  sub outerh { ('p', h()) }
    print join("|", sort(outerh()));  perl 1|k|p   PCL HASH(0x5)|p

  and the shape that WORKS, which localises it:
    sub deep { my @r = (1, inner()); @r }
    print join("|", deep());      perl 1|1|2   PCL 1|1|2

MECHANISM (measured, not guessed).  A comma list whose elements include a call
or an array is emitted as a LIST TEMP -- a simple vector whose aggregate
elements are left UNFLATTENED, with the expansion deferred to the consumer.
Two consumers exist and they disagree:

  * %p-flatten-list / %p-flatten-list-general (list assignment, foreach) walks
    RECURSIVELY -- its vector arm is `(loop for x across item do (add x))` and
    its hash arm expands to pairs.  That is why `my @l = D1->steps` and
    `foreach my $step (D1->steps)` are both CORRECT.
  * p-flatten-args (the ARGUMENT list -- @_, and therefore join/print/any user
    call) spreads exactly ONE level: a nested vector element becomes
    `(%p-elem-cell arg j)`, i.e. a BOX over the nested vector = an arrayref,
    which stringifies as ARRAY(0x N).  A p-flatten-marker element is not
    expanded at all and prints as the raw struct.

So the bug is that ONE of the two flatteners implements perl's list flattening
and the other implements a single-level spread, and which one a program gets
depends on whether the list reaches an assignment/foreach or an argument list.

WHY IT MATTERS.  `qw(a b), $obj->SUPER::method` is not exotic -- it is exactly
Role::Tiny/Moo::Role's `role_application_steps`, and any `sub f { (X, g()) }`
consumed by join/print/a user sub hits it.  The value printed is a reference,
so it is SILENT: no warning, no die, plausible-looking output.

FIX SHAPE (not designed).  Either p-flatten-args recurses like
%p-flatten-list-general does (measure: it is the hottest path in the runtime,
and the recursion must not cost the common all-scalar call anything -- the same
trade %p-args-need-flatten already had to make), or the emitter stops producing
un-flattened list temps in a RETURN/argument position.  Read
docs/ir-spec.md Â§5.3's shape table first: the ARRAY-vs-LIST-TEMP distinction is
now normative there (task #964), and any fix must keep it.

BAR: the six rows above on both emission paths; the `deep` row and every
foreach/list-assign row unmoved; corpus-diff + a full sweep (this is the
argument path, so everything reaches it).
subject: PRE-EXISTING silent-wrong: a NESTED aggregate in a returned list is not flattened by the ARGUMENT path -- join("|", D1->steps) gives ARRAY(0x1) where perl gives the elements
